title: Candles that tell a story
desc: Hammer, doji and engulfing: the candles worth a second look

cards.title: After a long fall
cards.situation: The price fell for four days. Then this candle: a small body near the top and a long lower wick. What might it tell you?

chart.label: Four falling days, then a candle with a small body near the top and a long lower wick down to $90

options.feedback: Sellers pushed it down to $90, but buyers pulled it most of the way back.

options.text: Buyers fought back from the lows
options.feedback: That long lower wick is buyers fighting back. It’s called a [[hammer|hammer]].
Each candle records the day’s fight. A long lower wick after a fall shows buyers pushed back hard.

cards.work: Low $90, close $97.50: buyers pushed price back up $7.50 from the low.

cards.title: Three shapes worth knowing
cards.text: Most candles mean little on their own. These three are worth a second look.

items.name: Hammer
items.text: Long lower wick after a fall. Buyers fought back.

items.name: Doji
items.text: Opens and closes at the same price. Nobody won.

items.name: Engulfing
items.text: A big green body swallows the red one before it.

cards.title: A bullish engulfing
cards.text: After a fall, a green candle **opens below** yesterday’s close and **closes above** yesterday’s open. Its body swallows the red one.

chart.label: Three falling days, a small red candle, then a big green candle whose body swallows it

cards.foot: Buyers took over the whole day. It’s a clue the fall may pause, not a promise.

cards.title: One candle, big promise?
cards.myth: A hammer means the price will go up.
cards.reality: One candle is a clue, not a signal. It matters only in the right place, like after a fall or at a level, and when the next candle agrees.
cards.rule: wait for the next candle to confirm before you act.

cards.title: Spot the doji
cards.q: Which candle shows that buyers and sellers ended the day even?

options.feedback: Candle A is a hammer: small body, long lower wick. A doji opens and closes at almost the same price.
Open and close at almost the same price: neither side won the day. That’s a [[doji|doji]].
A long green body: buyers won that day. A doji opens and closes at almost the same price.
A long red body: sellers won that day. A doji opens and closes at almost the same price.

cards.title: Wrong place
cards.q: A hammer shows up in the middle of a quiet, sideways week. No fall came before it. What does it tell you?

options.feedback: A hammer means buyers fought back after a fall. With no fall before it, there was nothing to fight back from.

options.text: Not much: shapes matter where they appear
options.feedback: A hammer means something after a fall or at a level. In a quiet sideways week, it carries little weight.
Nothing here says sell. It’s one candle in a quiet week, not a reason to act.
One candle in a sideways week can’t turn a trend. There was no trend to turn.

cards.headline: You can spot the candles worth a second look.
lines: Hammer: buyers fought back after a fall.
Doji: open and close the same, nobody won.
One candle is a clue, never a signal on its own.
